personality.description: This person usually sticks to familiar routines, prefers proven methods, and may resist suggestions that feel overly novel or untested. They keep life reasonably organized without being rigid, and they can adapt when needed, though they tend to choose the path that is most predictable. In moral dilemmas, they are likely to weigh outcomes in a practical, self-protective way and may be skeptical of others’ claims about what is fair or right, especially if those claims seem to conflict with their own interests. In group discussions, they speak in a measured but sometimes guarded manner, often questioning assumptions, challenging weak arguments, and focusing on concrete points rather than broad idealism.
traits: has assertively moved up the ranks into positions of leadership
prioritizes having control and authority over others
makes quick and definitive decisions, and once a decision is made it is usually final
has their own views of how tasks should be accomplished
uses reward and punishment to get people to follow their ideas
